Melanoma Breakthrough - Immunotherapy

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A Medical Breakthrough, a cure for stage 4 Melanoma cancer

Summary:
Melanoma Breakthrough

In a medical and scientific breakthrough a new drug has been tried and tested which offers a cure for the deadly melanoma cancer. This is specifically aimed at cancer patients with Stage 4 melanoma and for whom chemotherapy has not helped. We profile two stage 4 melanoma patients who have been on this cutting edge new treatment and have been declared cancer free. So what is different, it’s the way the drug instead of operating like chemotherapy targets the actual body immune system building it up to fight the cancer. This is leading the way for other cancer drugs to possibly go the same route.


Further information:
Melissa Taylors story is one of hundreds we and other forms have media, has shown time and time again. In 2006 she noticed a black spot on the base of her foot, but being she had other things on her mind and so forgot about it. Six months later the spot had grown to the size of a R2 coin..and still she did nothing. A year later the spot had become an irritant and so during a routine check up she asked her Dr to look at it….and very quickly it was confirmed this was a lethal melanoma.

Within two weeks Melissa’s whole life had changed, she had seen drs, oncologists, had two operations and undergone chemotherapy . Despite all this the cancer had spread and in November 2006 she was diagnosed with Stage 4 Melanoma and given 6 months to live.

In the past this was the end of the road and that’s what Melissa though she cashed in her savings and took her daughter to Disney land.

Bu on her return, everything changed and the tragic story that was to be Melissa’s became one of hope. Melissa became the first South African to get on a global clinical trial for immunotherapy for advanced Melanoma courtesy of Dr Vorobiof. Oncologist and Director of Sandton Medical Centre.

The difference with this treatment is unlike chemo which kills the cancer, this drug called Ipilmumab builds up the immune system to fight the cancer.

Now the drug Ipilimumab ( developed by Bristol – Myers Squibb) has now been approved for use in South Africa for by the Medicines Control Council.
Taylor had four infusions of the immunotherapy drug – four infusions costs between a quarter million to a million depending on the size of the patient
Survival rate of those with advanced melanoma goes from zero to 25% with the use of this drug
The treatment of malignant melanoma has remained virtually unchanged for 30 years, but the arrival of drugs that target the genetic structure of tumour cells, and the immunodrug Ipilimumab, which encourages the body's own immune system to fight the cancer, have radically altered the approach taken to those suffering advanced skin cancer. It is real medical break through and will affect treatment and drug development of other cancers
Lynette van Schalkwyk is another success story, she was only 31 when she was diagnosed with advanced melanoma, despite having it removed, eight years later a 9 tcm umor was discovered on her ovary….Worse still it had spread. Chemotherapy had no affect and Lynettes own Dr put her on the immunotherapy treatment, ten months later she was clean.

Press Release:


Melanoma Breakthrough
When Melissa Taylor was diagnosed with advanced malignant melanoma, her daughter was only a year old. It was unlikely she would see her grow up. But the fact that this sort of cancer is very closely linked to the immune system, would become her saving grace. Carte Blanche investigates an innovative new drug that treats advanced Melanoma by recruiting the body’s own immune system to specifically fight cancer cells.


Script:


V/O 7 sec

When Melissa Taylor, was diagnosed with Malignant Melanoma, her daughter Ayrin was only a year old.

Melissa: I did not think I would ever see my child grow up because once I had started reading the statistics about melanoma I was given a 2 % chance of survival 2% we are not talking 30/40 so I started writing letters so for all her milestones what Id say to her when she was 16, her 21st and I remember writing those letters at the time the first couple of letters just had tears all over and I had to keep re writing the letter

V/O 19 sec

Malignant Melanoma is one of the most aggressive of cancers. The main cause is over exposure to the sun’s UVA rays and in South Africa with our sunny skies and outdoor lifestyle, protection is essential. Despite several surgeries and18 session of chemotherapy Melissa’s cancer spread.

Melissa: It’s diff when someone says you have cancer in your foot you have a lot more hope, but the fact that it had spread to all four quadrants of my liver and two nodes of my lung was that’s it .. how much time it was around a bout 6 months
Gavin: The Dr right at the beginning said Melanoma can be contained but if it spreads we don’t know what to do about it.

Daniel Vorobiof: The best results we had with chemo was in 10/15 % of the patient, so that means that 85 % of patients never responded.

V/O 14 sec
Daniel Vorobiof is a leading oncologist in South Africa and for the last 30 years has been involved in researching treatment that has a better success rate than chemo for people with Malignant Melanoma.

Dr Vorobiof: The situation changed when it was understood that MM is a very immunogenic type of cancer, closely intertwined with the immune system

V/0 12 sec
And so the quest was on for a drug that, unlike chemotherapy which kills cancer and other cells indiscriminately, instead strengthens the bodies immune system to fight the cancer.

Daniel Vorobiof: 10/12 yrs ago that that mechanism was found in the USA by a group of scientists and immediately as they found a way that they can block the cells to allow the immune system the T cells as we call them to activate and fight for our problem, it was only then that they found the drug that can do that

LINK
Ipilimubag is a breakthrough drug for malignant melanoma one treatment is all it takes and that consists of just four infusions and if it works it really works.

V/O 15 sec
In December 20006, Melissa, still reeling from the shock that chemo hadn’t worked, suddenly had another shot at life. Clinical trials for this new immunotherapy drug, had began.

Melisa: I was the right candidate, I was the right blood type, I had been on previous chemo’s before. I was extremely lucky at that point in time.

V/O 7 sec
And Melissa became a guinea pig for the first clinical trials, of Ipilimumab.

Claire: Were you scared?
Melissa : I was all in, I had got so used to the hectic drugs that I had been on that I felt it could not get worse so I was prepared to be sick if that was what it meant, whatever it took is what I would do.

V/O 10 sec
Seven years down the line, wife and mother of two small boys Lynette van Schaik, was also in the right place at the right time.

Link
In Jan 2013 Lynette was diagnosed with MM stage four, she immediately started chemotherapy. The side effects were debilitating she experienced intense nausea, extreme pain and sensitivity to light. At the next check instead of finding out that cancer was reduced she was devastated to find out cancer had spread throughout her body.

Lynette: When I saw the Dr had said if something drastic does not happen he gives me six months to a year, and I said no I am not taking that I am going to fight this thing I am going to do this for my kids and when the cancer spread with me being on chemo I sat there in front of the Dr and she said to me this it there is nothing else we can do for you.

V/O 10 sec
But there was something, the third phase of the clinical trials had begun. Lynette was an ideal candidate, she was in Stage 4 and Chemo had failed.

V/O 11 sec
Bernado Rapaport, an oncologist working with Dr Vorobiof, saw that the spread of Lynette’s cancer would test the power of this new immunotherapy treatment.

Bernado Rapaport: Immunotherapy doesn’t work on all the patients but when it works it works for a long time
Claire: Why not work on some patients?
Bernado : That’s how it is, we can tell that it is likely that it will work or if its unlikely here with most of the studies are show that you can get 20/25 % doable remissions.

V/O 14 sec
Without immunotherapy survival rate is zero, so that’s a big leap forward… In 2006 when Melissa was one of the first on the trial there was a lot that was unknown.

Daniel Vorobiof, You’re scared because it is a completely diff thing because you don’t know how a patient is going to respond you don’t know what the toxic side effects will be of that patient so you really have to be alert all the time.
Melissa: I was either going to be around for 6 months or I cd be part of clinical trial and possibly die from side effects but would rather have the risk and the reward afterwards than not take risk at all.

V/O 8 sec
The side effects for Melissa were severe, extreme diahreara, , nausea vomiting and a skin condition called vitilligo.

Dr Vorobief: After the second cycle she landed in hospital. We had to treat her intensively then clause said that if patient has what we call a Grade 4 toxicity then the patient cannot continue on the treatment because if it happen again the patient might die
Melissa: It wasn’t my choice I was prepared it didn’t matter how sick I was or how debilitated I was I wanted the 4 treatments because I wanted to survive.

V/O 11 sec
But the ruling came, Melissa was withdrawn from the trials, her last hope gone, so what did she do she cashed in her Life Insurance Policy and took her family to Disney land.

Gavin: There was an attempt to make it as fun as possible there but I think on the back of your head it’s always what if this is the last one.

V/O 7 sec
For Lynette, the experience was so much easier, her side effects virtually nil.

Claire: So how soon did you start to feel better?
Lynette: Almost immediately, I was being sneaky I cd feel lump going smaller and smaller but was not telling anyone except the Dr I wasn’t telling anyone else.

V/O 7 sec
Eight months after being diagnosed with cancer, 12 weeks after immunotherapy treatment ,Lynette was cancer free.

Dr Rapoport : We didn’t know if she was going to respond in fact when she started the treatment, she was very sick and she had a dramatic response and she is still responding to the treatment.

V/O 12 sec
On her return from Disneyland, Melissa went for a check up. Even though she had received, only half the treatment, the X Ray was clear.

Claire: How was it receiving that news?
Melissa: As a patient one of the biggest things you fear is getting the results there is nothing on earth that explains the feeling like that once you get given the death sentence the next minute you are cancer free.

V/O 10 sec
For Melissa and Lynette this somewhat miracle drug was free, they were guinea pigs. Now that Ipilimumbab has been launched commercially, the cost is a million rand .

Dr Vorobiof: I cannot defend those prices I feel very uncomfortable also and unfortunately we cannot talk about a good drug because there is only one type of good drug the one that a patient can afford
Dr Rapoport: I’m not sure how long it will take for the prices to come down but some of the medical aids are looking at diff models on how to reimburse the drug.
Dr Vorobiof : There is a major effort world wide because drugs are becoming too expensive. So I believe there has to be some form of understanding between those that produce drugs, those that consume drugs and the authorities in between.

V/O
Lynette’s been cancer free for just under 2 years, Melissa 9 years, both had zero chance of survival …in all probability this will change the way we treat cancer in the future.

Dr Rapoport : This is a new concept of not giving chemo to kill cancer but give new system to fight the cancer///this will change dramatically in the next 10 years the way we are going to be treating patients.

Dr Vorobiof : Today the use of chemo still rep 90% of all treatments in another 15 years that will be around 10 to 15 % and there will be all these new drugs coming through.
